rationale: RSN StitchBank says cross stitch consists of two straight crossing stitches (line 40); direct and uniquely matches the X clue. Adjacent chain-stitch candidate is separately defined by linked loops, so no answer leak.
RSN StitchBank says chain stitch is a series of interlocking loops, each held by the next (line 34); distinguishes it from the neighboring X-shaped cross stitch.
Merriam-Webster bead definition 2 (line 56) explicitly gives a small material piece pierced for threading on string/wire; uniquely separates bead from pendant/clasp/jump ring.
Merriam-Webster pendant definition 1a (lines 54–60) defines a necklace ornament allowed to hang free. The jewelry-context qualifier avoids the broader senses; distinct from bead, clasp and jump ring.
Merriam-Webster clasp noun 1a (lines 42–45) says a device holds objects or parts together. Closing the two ends of a bracelet is distinct from the openable linking jump ring specified in 081.
Fire Mountain Gems, “Jump Rings—The Basics” (lines 45–50): wire coil cut into rings with a slit; typical use is connection/linking. The slit ring clue uniquely distinguishes this finding from clasp.
